sections.content:
Population change in Wakefield in 2032

The population in Wakefield is projected to increase from 357,698 people in 2022 to 390,301 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 28,654 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Wakefield
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Wakefield, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 2,701, with 36,729 births and 39,430 deaths in Wakefield between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Wakefield by 0.8%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 28,654, with 159,870 people moving to the area and 131,216 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Wakefield by 8.0%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 490, with 2,886 people moving to the area and 3,376 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Wakefield by 0.1%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 6,703, with 16,092 people moving to the area and 9,389 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Wakefield by 1.9%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Wakefield in 2032

The median age in Wakefield is projected to rise from 41 years in 2022 to 42 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 20% of the population in Wakefield are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 18% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Wakefield between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Wakefield is projected to stay the same, at around 63%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 283 to 288 over the same time period.

This is around average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Wakefield?

In 2032, 20% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 22% in 2022.

This is the same as the average for England in 2032.

Looking at the youngest age groups in Wakefield between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 7%
